hypothesis: The upper candle shadow (high minus max of open/close) represents failed bullish attempts. Persistent upper shadows signal overhead selling pressure and a bearish short-term outlook.
The lower candle shadow (min of open/close minus low) represents rejected bearish attempts and buying support. Large lower shadows signal strong demand at price lows and bullish reversal potential.

hypothesis: Overnight price gaps normalized by dynamic 10-day return volatility represent pure dislocation signals. By applying a 75% liquidity gate and a smooth 6-day decay, we minimize turnover and maximize risk-adjusted payout.
Extreme price displacement from VWAP normalized by intraday range measures session stretch on high volume. Reversion captures fade to mean value.
Short-term cumulative return momentum normalized by dynamic 10-day return volatility identifies market-independent exhaustion points.
Comparing open position vs close position within daily high-low channel on large volume exposes early-session buyer traps that mean-revert.
